examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Product of a Complex Number and Its Conjugate
examples.worked_solution:
*Method 1*

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=7-4\textrm{i},$ the real part is $\textrm{Re}(z)=7,$ and the imaginary part is $\textrm{Im}(z)=-4,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & ={7}^{2}+(-4)^{2} \\  & =49+16 \\  & =65.\end{aligned}
$$

*Method 2*

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=7-4\textrm{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overline{z} = 7 + 4 \textrm{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(7-4\text{i})(7+4\text{i}) \\  & ={7}^{2}+(7)(4)\text{i}+(-4)(7)\text{i}-(4)^{2}{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & =49+28\text{i}-28\text{i}-(16)(-1) \\  & =49+16 \\  & =65.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=-8+2\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=-8,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(-8) \\  & =-16.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-8+2\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-8-2\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(-8+2\text{i})+(-8-2\text{i}) \\  & =(-8+(-8))+\text{i}(2-2) \\  & =-16+\text{i}0 \\  & =-16.\end{aligned}
$$
